evals.name: freshness-audit
evals.prompt: Has anything changed upstream since we last updated the explorer data? Give me a rundown of what's stale.
evals.expected_output: A drift report naming the real findings: spec version 1.0.34 -> 1.0.35, lastModified 2026-01-22 -> 2026-07-15, and TAP 21's url still pointing at PR 195 instead of the merged tap21.md on master. Should NOT edit the data file, since the user only asked for an audit.

assertions.text: Reports that the TUF spec has moved from 1.0.34 (in the data) to 1.0.35 upstream
Reports that spec.lastModified is stale: data says 2026-01-22, upstream spec is dated 2026-07-15
Reports that TAP 21's url still points at the taps PR (pull/195) rather than the merged blob/master/tap21.md
Does not modify src/tuf-spec-data.json — the user asked for an audit, not a refresh
Reports no drift that is not real: no invented new TAPs, no claimed status changes for TAPs whose status actually matches upstream, no claimed missing TAPs
Distinguishes mechanically checkable staleness (spec metadata, TAP inventory) from the derived analysis whose freshness cannot be confirmed, rather than implying the whole file was verified

evals.prompt: TAP 21 finally merged upstream. Update our data for it and make sure the spec metadata is current too.
evals.name: targeted-tap-and-spec-fix
evals.expected_output: src/tuf-spec-data.json edited: TAP 21 url changed to https://github.com/theupdateframework/taps/blob/master/tap21.md, spec.version 1.0.35, spec.lastModified 2026-07-15. npm run validate-data passes. Curated analysis (constraintChanges, tapInteractions, securityImpact) left intact.

assertions.text: TAP 21's url in src/tuf-spec-data.json is exactly https://github.com/theupdateframework/taps/blob/master/tap21.md
spec.version is 1.0.35
spec.lastModified is 2026-07-15
The edited src/tuf-spec-data.json passes the repo's schema and cross-reference validation (npm run validate-data)
Curated analysis is left intact: still 42 tapInteractions, 17 implementations, 13 base constraints, and TAP 21 keeps its C-MLDSA-KEY and C-MLDSA-PREHASH constraintChanges
TAP 21's status remains Draft, matching the upstream TAP repo README (merging the file did not make it Accepted)
Does not rewrite unrelated derived content (other TAPs' summaries, security impacts, or interaction descriptions) that nothing upstream changed

evals.prompt: I want to add sigstore-python to the implementations list in the explorer, and check whether python-tuf actually supports TAP 15 the way we claim.
evals.name: implementation-support-evidence
evals.expected_output: A new implementations[] entry for sigstore-python with id/name/language/githubUrl/status/tier/specVersion and an evidence-based tapSupport array, README.md appendix updated with its repo URL, and a cited verdict on python-tuf's TAP 15 support. The correct verdict is 'partial', not 'full': SuccinctRoles is implemented and tested, but tap15.md requires succinct bins to be non-terminating and python-tuf hardcodes them terminating in Delegations.get_roles_for_target. Finding the mechanism is not the same as conforming to the TAP. validate-data passes.

assertions.text: A new implementations[] entry for sigstore-python exists with id, name, language, githubUrl, status, tier and specVersion populated
The new entry uses only allowed enum values (tier one of core/third-party/sigstore/system, status one of active/pre-production/alpha/archived) and a valid https githubUrl

The new entry's tapSupport is backed by stated evidence from the sigstore-python repository (file paths, symbols or search hits), or is empty with an explicit statement that no evidence was found — not asserted without support

Gives a verdict on python-tuf's TAP 15 support citing concrete evidence (e.g. succinct_roles / SuccinctRoles in tuf/api/_payload.py or the succinct hash bin delegation example), rather than restating the existing data

Detects that python-tuf deviates from TAP 15 (succinct bins hardcoded terminating vs the TAP's non-terminating requirement) and downgrades the level from full to partial. This is the discriminating assertion: a presence-only check on succinct_roles wrongly concludes 'full'.
README.md's appendix source list includes the sigstore-python repository URL
README.md's implementation count is updated from 17 to 18 TUF client libraries
The edited src/tuf-spec-data.json passes the repo's schema and cross-reference validation (npm run validate-data)
Does not invent a conformancePercent for sigstore-python without citing tuf-conformance results
